exposure: Alport syndrome (X-linked, autosomal, severe variants, less severe variants)
Baseline eGFR (< 90 ml/min/1.73 m2 vs. normal renal function)
outcome: Pregnancy complications (high blood pressure, abortion, preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, nephrotic syndrome, cervical insufficiency with fetal growth delay, premature rupture of membranes, acute intrauterine fetal distress)
cohort: The study included 74 women with Alport syndrome (82% X-linked, 11% autosomal) from China and Europe, with detailed pregnancy information available for 62 pregnancies from 52 women.
finding: Women with Alport syndrome experience a significant increase in proteinuria during pregnancy and a decrease in eGFR after pregnancy, with those having severe variants or pre-existing eGFR below 90 ml/min/1.73 m2 facing greater risks of kidney disease progression.
